# Sheet 2: static timing at the final pin assignment (gate G-STA)

**Revision A1, 2026-11-19.** Re-run after the owner's G-SHEET2 review: C-26 (option C-17b) removed the LED_FAULT pin, which re-placed the design. The revision A figures are kept in §6 for comparison.

**Tool and command:** Lattice Diamond 3.14.0.75.2 (free licence), on the owner's PC. `bash hdl/syn/run_diamond.sh <work dir> <device>`; set `Z2_TOP=fit_top` for the fit test.

**Pins:** the LOCATE block in [../../hdl/syn/z2_top.lpf](../../hdl/syn/z2_top.lpf), generated by `tools/fpga/pinplan.py` and frozen against the G-SHEET2-approved assignment (only pin 67 changed). The fit test adds [../../hdl/syn/fit_top_extra.lpf](../../hdl/syn/fit_top_extra.lpf). The LPF of every run is the committed file.

**RTL:** rev A1. `z2_top` exposes `LED_READY` only. The core is unchanged.

> **What this closes and what it does not.**
> - **Closes:** the "final pin assignment and STA including the complete /SLAVEn path" part of G-STA (owner open requirement 1).
> - **Still open:**
>   - the host SPI capture path, once the SPI slave exists (sheet 4, HL-1 to HL-6);
>   - the comparison with M-1, M-2 and M-7 on hardware;
>   - a rerun at every later RTL or pin change. §6 shows that a one-pin change moved the figures by up to 0.8 ns.

> **Rounding rule (owner refinement 4).** Values quoted to fewer decimals than the tool reports are rounded in the conservative direction:
> - delays and requirements are rounded **up**;
> - slacks and margins are rounded **down**.
>
> Revision A had quoted the M-7 criterion as 19.2 ns for a requirement of 19.24 ns. That was rounded the wrong way and is corrected here.

## 1. Conditions

Unchanged from [sheet1-sta-results.md](sheet1-sta-results.md) §1:
- −4 grade, commercial (TJ 85 °C) and industrial (TJ 100 °C; map `-oc Industrial`);
- 15 pF on every output;
- LVCMOS33 on every port;
- both edges analysed;
- minimum delays from the fast model.

**Pad check:** passed on every run (every port LVCMOS33, every bank at VCCIO 3.3 V).

## 4. Hazard inequality (C-02) and the M-7 pass criterion

The buffer-skew term is 3.5 ns (sheet 1 §4).

| Quantity | Revision A1 runs | Envelope of every 2000HC placement analysed (rev A and rev A1) |
|---|---|---|
| **S_req conservative** (slow max − fast min) | 3.5 + (14.910 − 2.399) = 16.011 → **16.02 ns** | max(16.239, 16.011) → **16.24 ns** |
| S_req same corner (worst run) | 9.946 → **9.95 ns** | max(9.745, 9.946) → **9.95 ns** |
| Slot address hold | 3.5 + (8.597 − 2.726) = 9.371 → **9.38 ns** | max(9.600, 9.371) → **9.60 ns** |

**M-7 pass criterion (owner refinement 4).** The STA figures move with every re-place: rev A to rev A1 moved S_req by 0.23 ns. So the criterion is taken from the **envelope** of every placement analysed, not from the latest run.

| Criterion | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| **M-7, 2000HC (planning value)** | **≥ 19.3 ns** | 16.239 + 3 = 19.239, rounded up |
| M-7, same-corner basis | ≥ 13.0 ns, recorded as such | 9.946 + 3 = 12.946, rounded up |
| M-7, 4000HC fallback | **≥ 19.8 ns** | 16.709 + 3 = 19.709, rounded up (§5) |
| Hold | ≤ 9.6 ns needed; the MC68000 gives ≥ 40 ns (#13) [V S57] | – |

**How M-7 is judged:**
1. Take the **minimum** measured slot setup, minus the instrument's timing uncertainty, and compare it with the criterion.
2. Before the measurement, **re-derive the criterion from the STA of the exact bitstream under test.** Use whichever is larger: that value or the planning value above.
3. Record the bitstream's S_req with the result.

The same criterion applies to M-12 (PiStorm/Emu68 and other masters).

**R-43 (50 MHz):** worst slack 3.11 ns, against a 1 ns trigger. Rev A showed 3.91 ns at the same logic, so placement alone moves it by about 0.8 ns; keep tracking it at every run.

Both runs: **0 setup / 0 hold errors, pad check PASS.**

| ZB_A[23:16] → ZF_XRDY, slowest | 18 | 14.993 | 14.093 |
| → ZF_DBUF_OE_N, slowest (/UDS) | 18 | 14.534 | 12.614 |
| ZB_CFGIN_N → ZF_CFGOUT_N | 25 | 10.972 | 10.363 |
| 50 MHz slack | ≥ 0 | **3.859** | 4.892 |
| Clock-to-out SRAM_OUT / LD_OUT (max) | 12 / 16 | 10.450 / 12.915 | 9.951 / 13.259 |
| /SLAVEn at the slot | 35 | 20.33 ns | 20.43 ns |
| S_req conservative: these runs / envelope with rev A | – | 15.86 ns / **16.71 ns** | |

**The fallback meets every constraint at these pins:**
- worst Zorro path 14.993 ns, so slack ≥ 3.00 ns;
- 50 MHz slack ≥ 3.85 ns;
- M-7 criterion if the 4000HC is fitted: **≥ 19.8 ns**.

**If the 4000HC is bought:** rerun the industrial grade, then re-derive the criterion for the bitstream under test.

## 6. Revision A for comparison (2026-11-19, superseded)

102 signals (LED_FAULT still on pin 67); same method.

**2000HC:**
- worst Zorro path 15.094 ns;
- /AS → /SLAVEn 8.882 ns, so 20.682 ns at the slot;
- S_req 16.239 ns;
- 50 MHz slack 3.916 ns.

**4000HC:**
- worst 15.850 ns;
- S_req 16.709 ns;
- slack 3.601 ns.

Rev A had quoted M-7 as "≥ 19.2 ns"; corrected in §4.

The changes from rev A to rev A1 come from re-placement only. The logic is identical apart from the removed output.

## 7. Warnings

Same classes as revision A:
- ZB_E7M has no load;
- `ld_dout` initial values are ignored;
- the asgate VCC/GND nets have no load;
- there is no .sdc file;
- host-path registers are stuck at constants while `z2_hostif_stub` ties the host port off.

The fault indication (`fault_ind`) has no load until the sheet-4 host status word exists, so synthesis removes its logic.

**Warning comparison:** each run's Diamond warnings were compared by normalised message class with the matching revision A run. All six runs: **0 new classes, 0 removed**.
